Ashwini Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 2 September, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148287003/
1

C.S.C. 
 Court No. - 29
 Hon'Ble Mahesh Chandra Tripathi, J. 
Hon'Ble Anish Kumar Gupta, J.

1. Heard Sri R.B. Yadav, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri Ambrish Shukla, learned
Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State respondents.
2.

The instant writ petition is preferred commanding the respondents to enter the name of petitioner in place of Rajkiya Polytechnic in the revenue records over Gata No. 228 area 1.69 hectare situate in Village Kasba, Pargana, Tehsil and District-Etawah in pursuance of orders dated 13.8.2015 and 5.5.2016.
Further it is prayed that the representation of the petitioner dated 19.2.2025 be decided by the respondent authorities.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is bhumidhar of land bearing Gata No. 228 admeasuring 1.69 hectare situate in Village Kasba, Pargana, Tehsil and District-Etawah,
which was purchased by his mother, Smt. Om Radhika Devi vide sale deed dated 6.10.1980.

The State Government decided to acquire the land of the petitioner and as such issued notification under Section 4(1)/17(4) and Section 6/17(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 31.7.1982 and 6.8.1982, respectively.

It is submitted that mother of the petitioner challenged both the notifications by filing Writ C No. 7972 of 1984 (Smt. Om Radhika Devi vs. State of U.P. and others) and during the pendency of said writ petition petitioner's mother Smt. Om Radhika Devi died on 28.7.1985 and vide order dated 6.4.2015 name of petitioner as well as other legal heirs were substituted.

entities.text: Om Radhika Devi vs. State of U.P. and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said writ petition was disposed of vide order dated 13.8.2015 giving liberty to the petitioner to make representation before the competent authority.

4. He further submits that similarly situated other tenure holders also instituted separate petitions,
one of them being Writ C No. 12138 of 1982 (Balvir Singh and others vs. State of U.P. and others),
wherein the Division Bench by judgement and order dated 5.5.2016 had opined the invocation of urgency clause under Section 17(1) and 17(4) of the Act, 1894 were misuse of process and the dispensation of an enquiry under Section 5A of the Act, 1894 was unsustainable. Accordingly, the invocation of urgency clause under the Act, 1894 was set aside and the writ petition was partly allowed giving leave to the respondents, in case they still require the land in dispute, they may proceed from the stage of making enquiry under Section 5-A of the Act, 1894 after giving public notice to landowners, inviting objections and thereafter, take appropriate action as permissible in law.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the judgement and order dated 5.5.2016 was challenged before the Apex Court in Special Leave to Appeal (C) No. 18354 of 2019 (State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors. vs. Balbir Singh (Dead) Through Lrs. & Ors.).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same was dismissed by the Apex Court vide order dated 9.2.2022 on ground of delay.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner states that even though the petitioner's case was not connected along with Balvir Singh (Supra) but as there was separate order, wherein, the division Bench had disposed of the matter vide order dated 13.8.2015 giving leave to the petitioner, as the petitioner was already substituted in the said proceedings vide order dated 6.4.2015 to press the application/representation before respondents in the light of provisions contained under Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioner states that on one hand in the case of Balvir Singh (Supra) the invocation of urgency clause was set aside and leave was accorded to the respondents, in case the land was required for planned development the Authority can proceed to acquire from the stage of making enquiry under Section 5A of the Act, 1894 giving public notice to the landowners, inviting objections and on the other hand till date the Authority has not proceeded in view of the leave granted by the Division Bench.
Therefore, entire acquisition proceedings would lapse and direction may be issued to the respondent to restore the name of the petitioner in the revenue records by making the necessary entries.
5. In this backdrop, learned counsel for the petitioner has confined his relief that the application dated 19.2.2025 may be considered and decided by the authority concerned.
6. Considering the factual situation as placed before us, no useful purpose would be served in keeping the petition pending.

7. Taking into consideration the entire facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that interest of justice would be sub-served by issuing a direction to the second respondent to consider the cause of the petitioners and decide the representation of the petitioner dated 19.2.2025 in accordance with law within a period of six weeks from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
8. With the aforesaid direction, this writ petition is disposed of.
